note: Everything to build, in the order it will be done. On 13 Nov 2026 Jesse reviewed the demo and put three things first: RDF throughout, payment as a contract, and real runs behind every selector option; and paused benchmarking. Set by Jesse on 13 Nov 2026: the agent work first, then the paper, then zero-knowledge and joint computation, then the thesis, then adoption and the rest of the app suite. One gate, also set by Jesse: every use case and scenario marked "not run yet" becomes a real run, or is listed with the reason, before the last phases start. Careful thinking is done by Fable; building by Codex and Opus to Fable's briefs.

phases.title: RDF throughout, and every option a real run
phases.goal: From Jesse's review on 13 Nov 2026, now first in the order: meaning explicit at every gate, payment treated as a contract, and every option on every selector backed by a real run you can switch to on the mortgage journey. Of 38 alternative options, 13 have a real run somewhere in the use cases and 25 have none. On the mortgage journey none can be switched to as a real run today: the email trace shown there is a development fixture and is labelled as one. Done means: the journey runs under the baseline with that one option changed, between separately keyed agents, and one failure only that option can have also runs.

items.title: RDF through the pipeline: model, wire and gates
items.detail: One ontology with SHACL shapes and a JSON-LD context. Messages travel as JSON-LD under pinned contexts, every gate reads RDF through typed wrappers, statements and mandates become W3C Verifiable Credentials, terms stay ODRL. The baseline keeps a plain signature over the document; the Data Integrity option signs the canonical graph. Being built since 18:04 UTC on 13 Nov.

items.title: RDF in the stores, the record and the explorer
items.detail: Policies, memory, trust store and record held as RDF. Profiles and scenario files as JSON-LD. The inspector shows JSON-LD with the context folded away, and Turtle beside it.

items.title: Payment as a contract, with a selector at the point of payment
items.detail: A payment settles an agreement: the agent may pay only what a signed, accepted offer says is due, to the party it names, once. A paid valuation step is added to the mortgage journey. Options at the point of payment: a plain RDF description, x402, the Machine Payments Protocol, AP2 mandates and the Agentic Commerce Protocol, each lifted to the same RDF terms so the same checks run. Four failures: the amount differs, the payee differs, there is no offer behind it, and asked to look but not to buy. Designed (specification 18 updated); the build follows the RDF build.

items.title: Transport options
items.detail: A2A 1.0, MCP (revision 2026-07-28) and email as real runs of the mortgage journey, with a test that changing the transport changes no verdict. Each has a failure of its own, for example a readable copy of an email that says something different from the signed part. Designed; built with the configuration matrix right after the RDF build. Solid inbox comes with the Solid options.

items.title: Solid options
items.detail: One in-process storage that speaks the Solid Protocol, then: messages through an inbox, data by reference with a grant no wider than the terms, terms translated into access rules, the record mirrored to the person's own storage, and WebID. Designed.

items.title: Identity and authority options
items.detail: Decentralized identifier, email address as an endpoint, no identifier, mandate as a credential with a status list, grant from an authorization server, agent registry. Designed.

items.title: Authenticity and trust options
items.detail: Data Integrity proof (built with P9.1), served from the source's domain, selective disclosure, own list only, federation membership, trusted index with receipts, reputation. Designed.

items.title: Meaning and reliance options
items.detail: Registry lookup, negotiated meaning, plain language then upgrade, stated confidence, two sources must agree, certified quality. Designed.

items.title: Usage control, commitments and accountability options
items.detail: A model that may tighten the rules, human approval, agreement credential, claim to a regulator, fault passed to the vendor, public reputation, reputation score. Designed.

items.title: Proof of a query, and joint computation
items.detail: Zero-knowledge proofs use Noir circuits, not a virtual machine (Jesse, 13 Nov). The seam is built and tested with stand-in verifiers. The engine project's joint-computation package has arrived and is being wired in for six paths now. Six proof paths wait on its Noir package; three more wait on new circuits for absence and totals (targets: circuits 23 Nov, package 4 Dec). The queries it asked for were sent on 13 Nov.

phases.title: The reference agent and this explorer
phases.goal: A real agent built to the reference design, a site that replays what it did, and a narrated walkthrough.

items.title: Reference design
items.detail: Two gates around a black-box core, five inbound and six outbound checks, four stores, the verifiable message.

items.title: Check against OWASP, W3C and current practice
items.detail: Terms aligned; ten added requirements; see the Requirements view.

items.title: Explorer site
items.detail: Step-through and play modes, a selector per layer, message inspector, guided tour, use cases, evaluation. Public copy live at answerableagents.org.

items.title: Reference agent package
items.detail: Two gates, stores, a suite registry and a trace for every decision. Built; in review before merge (pull request 635).

items.title: Real traces: main flow and three failures
items.detail: The full 14-step flow with four parties running as agents, and three failures (the lender over-asks, an offer outside the limits, an injected instruction). All real runs, replayed in this explorer.

items.title: Swap the transport
items.detail: Direct transport and plain email both run through the same gates. The other transports are in the first section of this roadmap.

items.title: Product index and sector register
items.detail: Find lenders through a trusted index with no personal data; check them on a register.

items.title: Step-up challenge
items.detail: A bank asks for a certified face check before it accepts the mandate.

items.title: Joint computation as a data-sharing option
items.detail: Design and the seam are being built; the computation itself waits on packages from the engine project, due before 17 Nov.

items.title: Data by reference on Solid
items.detail: Grant read access in the pod and send a pointer with terms, instead of a copy.

items.title: When things go wrong
items.detail: Accountability flows you can switch between: a claim to a regulator, fault passed to the vendor, reputation.

items.title: Narrated walkthrough video
items.detail: First narrated version made. A re-record against the current site is owed.

items.title: Comparison with the agents already built
items.detail: The pilot, the suite agent and the policy sandbox drawn against the reference design, with gaps.

items.title: A core that is a real model
items.detail: AgentDojo with a real model as the core: 1,325 runs, five conditions, three attacks. See the Evaluation view.

phases.title: The specification family
phases.goal: One core document and a document per layer, written so someone else could implement them.

items.title: Core specification
items.detail: Roles, the verifiable message, the checks and their outcomes, the record, configurations.

items.title: Ten layer specifications
items.detail: For each layer: what a suite must define, and the suites registered so far.

items.title: Baseline configuration
items.detail: The recommended default, one suite per layer, so two strangers' agents can always talk.

items.title: Conformance
items.detail: The trace format, expected outlines, and the rule: no suite without a trace.

items.title: Mortgage profile
items.detail: The claims, accepted sources and assurance levels for the worked example.

items.title: Vocabulary
items.detail: Terms and reason codes as an ontology, governed on Concord.

items.title: Zero-knowledge query proof suite
items.detail: Drafted as an authenticity suite. Waits on the engine project for a proof that binds issuer and subject.

items.title: Derived data and inference
items.detail: Answers by query, by proof and by joint computation as one idea: a published rule applied to signed sources, with five ways of assuring the result.

items.title: Content that does not fit
items.detail: Rules for prose, pictures and judgement, in both directions: a model's reading is a new statement, and free text leaves unasked only when everything the model has seen could be sent.

phases.title: Use cases and evaluation
phases.goal: Show that the same design works across sectors and settings, say plainly where it does not, and measure it.

items.title: Catalog of use cases by context
items.detail: 70 use cases in 15 sectors and five settings, each with what makes it hard, what goes wrong and the expected outcome.

items.title: A real run for every use case
items.detail: 151 of 166 paths are real runs. The other 15 are listed by name: nine wait on a proof system, six on a joint computation.

items.title: Review of where the design fits and where it does not
items.detail: 13 kinds of case where messages in agreed terms fall short, what the design does about each, and what it leaves unsolved.

items.title: Evaluation plan
items.detail: Ten questions with a measure each, six methods, nine published benchmarks and how each maps onto the design.

items.title: Evaluation without a model
items.detail: Worst-case core, one-change and injected-fault runs: being built now. Paused on 13 Nov: benchmarking waits until the development above is done.

items.title: Benchmarks with a real model
items.detail: First run done with one model. Repeats, a second model and an attack written against the model are still to do.
